Back 4 Blood was something I approached with a mix of excitement and caution. I still had the sensations of Left 4 Dead in my hands, that game that stayed with me for years, almost like an old friend you never really forget. So of course, I was expecting it to slip up. And yet, within the first few minutes, I felt something familiar return — but with a rawer, more modern energy.
The chaos is still there, untouched, but denser. The weapons hit with a weight I hadn’t felt in a long time, and the infected swarm like a tide that refuses to let you breathe. What surprised me most was how the card system eventually won me over: at first I was skeptical, then I realized it gave each run its own identity, its own little story.
In co‑op, the game becomes something else entirely. You rediscover that simple joy of surviving together, of saving each other at the last second, of laughing after a total disaster. That’s where Back 4 Blood really grabbed me — in those moments where gameplay turns into a shared memory.
It’s not Left 4 Dead, and it doesn’t try to be. But it reminded me why I love this genre: the adrenaline, the camaraderie, the beautiful mess of it all. And in the end, I stopped comparing. I just enjoyed the ride.

Back 4 Blood is like Left 4 Dead 1 and 2, but there is a lot more to it than just that.

Just like in L4D, you can kill a lot of zombies, and you can find a lot of guns in the maps.

You collect supply points, for which you can get upgrade cards (called supply decks - which give you extras, such as more ammo, better armor etc.).
You can make your own deck with whatever you have found or bought with supply points.

Each playable toon (character) has a special ability, which can help your game a lot.
There are lots of cosmetic changes available for your toons and for your guns.
And, of course, there are special mutations.

If you play it on the hard setting, you will have a good challenge.

Finally, you can find supply crates in the maps that have special guns and accessories.
Some guns have special abilities, like incendiary ammo or slowing effect on zombies.

Back 4 Blood is fun, with progression and good graphics. It runs smoothly, and the shadow lighting is very well done.
All in all, it's a good game.

This game gets a weirdly bad shake considering it just takes what makes L4D2 work and updates and expands it. In pretty much every way, this is just a better version of L4D2.
It has a ton more replayability than L4D2, and I say that as someone who has dumped several hundred hours in the Left 4 Dead franchise. There are plenty of ways to recreate the feeling of the previous franchise, and the level design feels like an extension of the creativity shown off in L4D2.

If you want L4D2 but modernized with customization and some optional rogue-like modes, this is the game for you. Cross-platform multiplayer is a huge addition. The game is fun, saying otherwise feels ridiculous. The one weakness this game has versus previous entries is the character writing, but writing is never what we played these games for in the first place.

Overall, Back 4 Blood is a fun game (with friends), a good and challenging alternative to Left 4 Dead that offers variety and better combat mechanics. The card system is complex and confusing (i have one brain cell left). Buy only on sale and you won't regret it ;)

I don't exactly know why people hate this game so much.. It's quite decent , but it lacks the vibe that Left 4 Dead used to have. In exchange, there are so many new features it overwhelms new players and L4D fans alike.
1.Multiple Characters with Passive skills and different side arms.
2. Unlockable and interchangeable weapons accessories.
3. Unlockable Skill Cards to enchance multiple aspects like, Weapon damage, reload speed, running speed, stamina
4. New Currency in Copper to buy new skill cards and skins.
5. The (zombie) Ridden is faster, but their dying animation is a lot better than L4D.

But, honestly, for its price.. it doesn't worth 50$, more like 15-20$ worth of gaming pleasure experience.

A pale imitation of its successor, and other competitors in the genre. Everything from balance, level design, enemy design, weapon variety, and even the base combat system feels like a cheap copy of L4D2. Although the engine is very good, and the weapons feel alright, none of it comes close to capturing the magic or feel of similar games. The levels are laughably short, you can ACTUALLY sometimes see the END of the level, right from the start of them. Even a decade on, nothing seems to be able to take the lessons learned from L4D2. My advice would be to get World War Z, Vermintide 2, or just replay the classic instead. This game is not worth 60$
